By Lemma <REF_0001> an open immersion
is locally of finite type. A composition of morphisms locally of
finite type is locally of finite type
(Lemma <REF_0002>). Thus it is clear that if <MATH_0001> is
J-2 then any open and any scheme locally of finite
type over <MATH_0002> is J-2 as well. This proves the final
statement of the lemma.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
If <MATH_0003> is J-2, then for every finite type <MATH_0004>-algebra <MATH_0005>
the regular locus of the scheme <MATH_0006> is open. Hence <MATH_0007> is
J-2, by definition (see
More on Algebra, Definition <REF_0003>).
Combined with the remarks above we conclude that (1) implies (3), and
(2) implies (4). Of course (1) <MATH_0008> (2) and
(3) <MATH_0009> (4) trivially.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
To finish the proof we show that (4) implies (1).
Assume (4) and let <MATH_0010> be a morphism locally of finite type.
We can find an affine open covering <MATH_0011> such that
each <MATH_0012> maps into one of the <MATH_0013>. By
Lemma <REF_0004>
the induced ring map <MATH_0014> is
of finite type. Hence the regular locus of
<MATH_0015> is open. Since
<MATH_0016> we conclude that
<MATH_0017> is open as desired.
